subject: CK
correct: On a statin with muscle symptoms: CK <4× ULN → explore other causes, continue if tolerable (or pause 2–4 weeks and rechallenge); CK 4–10× ULN or intolerable symptoms → stop statin for 4–6 weeks, then reassess/rechallenge; CK ≥10× ULN → urgent same-day assessment (rhabdomyolysis is a clinical diagnosis: dark urine, AKI, severe weakness). The NICE NG238 5× ULN rule applies only BEFORE starting a statin (NHS England statin intolerance pathway; already adopted site-wide in LAB_SITE_FIXES batch 7).

fixes.old:
Myopathy (CK >5× ULN)

Rare (1-3 per 100,000 patient-years); stop statin; CK monitoring; usually resolves after cessation.
fixes.new:
Statin myopathy (CK 4–10× ULN or intolerable symptoms)

Severe myopathy is rare (1-3 per 100,000 patient-years); stop the statin for 4–6 weeks, then reassess and rechallenge (NHS England statin intolerance pathway); usually resolves after cessation.

fixes.old:
• CK 5-10× ULN: stop statin; confirm resolution; rechallenge with different statin after 4 weeks; monitor CK
  • CK >10× ULN (rhabdomyolysis): STOP IMMEDIATELY; IV fluids; monitor renal function; urgent medical review
fixes.new:
• CK 4–10× ULN or intolerable symptoms: stop statin for 4–6 weeks; confirm resolution; rechallenge at a lower dose or with a different statin; monitor CK
  • CK ≥10× ULN: STOP the statin; urgent same-day assessment; rhabdomyolysis (dark urine, AKI): hospital, IV fluids, monitor renal function

subject: HbA1c
correct: NICE NG28: individualised target; usually 48 mmol/mol (lifestyle or a single drug not causing hypoglycaemia), 53 mmol/mol on a drug that can cause hypoglycaemia; intensify if it rises to 58 mmol/mol; relax for frailty/limited life expectancy.

subject: HbA1c
correct: NG28 gives no fixed relaxed target; it advises relaxing targets for frailty/dementia individually.
note: cases/dementia.html states 'HbA1c target 58 mmol/mol (relaxed to 64 mmol/mol in frail elderly)' (lines 336, 763, 1702). 58 is NG28's intensification threshold, not a target, and 64 is not a national figure (some local/ADA/TREND guidance uses 58–70 for frail). Owner: keep as an example 'relaxed individual target (e.g. 58–64 mmol/mol, local/TREND-UK)' or reword to 'individualised relaxed target agreed with the patient/carer (NG28)'.

subject: HbA1c
correct: NICE NG28: continue a GLP-1 mimetic only if HbA1c falls by at least 11 mmol/mol (1.0%) AND weight falls by at least 3% of initial body weight at 6 months.

fixes.old: HbA1c + weight at 3 months — stop if no ≥1% HbA1c reduction or ≥3% weight loss at 6 months (NICE NG28 criterion)
fixes.new: HbA1c + weight at 3 months — continue beyond 6 months only if HbA1c has fallen ≥11 mmol/mol (1%) AND weight ≥3% (NICE NG28 criterion; when used for glucose/weight rather than CV benefit)

fixes.old: Stop if <1% (11 mmol/mol) HbA1c reduction at 6 months.
fixes.new: Continue at 6 months only if HbA1c has fallen ≥11 mmol/mol (1%) AND weight ≥3% (NICE NG28).

note: 'stop if no ≥1% reduction or ≥3% weight loss' reads as either criterion being enough; NICE requires both. The second card omits the weight criterion. assets/meds/type-2-diabetes.js and tools/prescribing.html already state it correctly.
